classification: Source-only scope assessment of explicit pelvis-gap coordinates; not a selected construction
source_result: Mechanics.calc forms the pelvis transform directly from root=(x,y,z0+dz*f) and R_s(p)=baseR_s*(I+sin(angle*p)*K+(1-cos(angle*p))*K^2). Pelvis gap does not directly depend on leg coordinates, arm angles or corner loads.

In exact real interpretation of those stored model parameters, gap_s=n_x*x+n_y*y+n_z*(z0+dz*f)+plane_d+min_v n^T*R_s(p)*v. It is affine in x,y,f at fixed p. The remaining nonlinearity and possible vertex switches depend on the one orientation coordinate p.
If n_z*dz is nonzero, this expression can solve f explicitly for a specified physical gap. No such denominator, branch, interval or numerical identity was evaluated on study arrays.
primary_scope_obstruction: The full original primary retains an independent auxiliary gap g and both signs of its consistency residual: |g-gap_linear|<=sigma_gap*t. The scalar t need not be zero.

Setting f from g alone imposes zero gap residual and restricts that primary domain; it is not an equivalent coordinate change of the whole minimax problem. No proof shows an original optimum on this restricted domain.

To retain the full domain one must retain an independent gap-error coordinate e, with gap=g-e and both signed bounds |e|<=sigma_gap*t. Replacing f by e does not itself remove a degree of freedom or establish computational savings.

Changing f after receiving a backend point would change the motion point and its coupled foot, arm, command, moment, torque and timing conditions. The earlier finite-map approval and named dual correction do not authorize that projection.
decision: Do not launch explicit gap projection or claim that the scalar formula solves the remaining cases. This source identity can inform a future construction, but a full-original witness/equivalence mechanism and useful cost reduction remain absent. Do not repeat the source derivation or inspect vertex branches generically on this basis.
